mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.25% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3% over three months signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressures and corporate costs, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE decreased by more than 0.3% over three months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real GDP by more than 2% over the previous quarter signals strong economic demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances where GDPC1 increased by more than 2% over the previous quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production by more than 1% over two months signals a supply shock, which increases input costs and reduces corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where INDPRO decreased by more than 1% over two months.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where a higher level of housing starts indicates stronger economic demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the correlation between HOUST levels and S&P 500 60-day forward returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) over any 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven signal where a combination of rising CPI and stable or decreasing federal funds rate suggests inflationary pressures without corresponding monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 1 month AND FEDFUNDS stable or decrease
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL increased by more than 0.5% and FEDFUNDS was stable or decreased.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven signal where a combination of increasing nonfarm payrolls and decreasing unemployment rate suggests a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressures and corporate costs, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 0.5% in 1 month AND UNRATE decrease > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where PAYEMS increased by more than 0.5% and UNRATE decreased by more than 0.2% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional signal where a decrease in real personal consumption expenditures signals a weakening demand environment, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, but only during a late-cycle expansion.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where RSAFS decreased by more than 1% in a month during a late-cycle expansion.
